answer: Sybil resistance starts with a stake that is refundable only after a long cool-down and is slashed the moment a duplicate identity is proven. To run N fake agents, an attacker must lock N stakes at once and lose every one on detection, so copying a keypair buys nothing while real capital does not duplicate. A saffron-priced registration surcharge makes each extra identity cost more than the last, and a bounded set of falcon verifier seats inspects shared payment trails, catching a cluster early. Like a reef growing by accretion, the identity set gets harder to forge over time.
